verses.text: "Be silent before me, you islands! Let the nations find new strength. Let them come near and speak. Let us meet together in court.

Who has stirred up a ruler from the east and called him in righteousness to serve him? God hands nations over to him and lets him conquer kings. His sword turns them to dust. His bow scatters them like straw in the wind.
He chases them and moves on safely, on a road his feet have never traveled.
Who has done this and made it happen? Who has called each generation from the beginning? I, the LORD, am the first, and I will be with the last. I am he."
The islands have seen it and are afraid. The ends of the earth tremble. They come near and gather together.
Each one helps the other and says to their friend, "Be strong!"

The craftsman encourages the goldsmith. The one who smooths metal with a hammer encourages the one who strikes the anvil. He says of the welding, "It is good." Then he fastens the idol with nails so that it will not fall over.
"But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, you descendants of my friend Abraham,
I took you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I said, 'You are my servant. I have chosen you and have not rejected you.'
So do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not be discouraged, for I am your God. I will make you strong and help you. I will hold you up with my victorious right hand.
Look, all who are angry with you will be ashamed and disgraced. Those who fight against you will become nothing and will die.
You will look for your enemies, but you will not find them. Those who make war against you will be as nothing at all.
For I am the LORD your God, who holds your right hand and says to you, 'Do not be afraid. I will help you.'
Do not be afraid, Jacob, you little worm, you people of Israel. I myself will help you," says the LORD. "Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I will make you like a new, sharp threshing sledge with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and make the hills like chaff.
You will toss them into the air, and the wind will carry them away. The storm will scatter them. But you will be glad in the LORD and boast in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy look for water, but there is none. Their tongues are dry with thirst. But I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not leave them.
I will make rivers flow on the bare hills, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into pools of water, and the dry ground into springs.
I will plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive trees in the wilderness. I will put cypress, fir, and pine trees together in the desert,
so that people will see and know, and think about it and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Present your case," says the LORD. "Bring your best arguments," says the King of Jacob.
"Let your idols come and tell us what is going to happen. Tell us what happened in the past, so we can think about it and know how it turned out. Or tell us what is coming in the future.
Tell us what will happen later, so that we will know you are gods. Do something, good or bad, so that we will be amazed and afraid together.
But look, you are less than nothing, and your works are worthless. Whoever chooses you is disgusting.
I have stirred up a ruler from the north, and he has come, a ruler from the east who calls on my name. He tramples rulers like mud, like a potter stomping clay.
Who told about this from the beginning, so we could know? Who told us before, so we could say, 'He was right'? No one told about it. No one announced it. No one heard any words from you.
I was the first to tell Zion, 'Look, here they are!' I sent a messenger to Jerusalem with good news.
When I look among the idols, there is no one, no adviser among them who can give an answer when I ask.
Look, they are all false! Their works are nothing. Their metal images are only wind and confusion."
